AEM Flex 120
_AEM Flex 120

The AEM Flex 120 is a skid-mounted, 120 kW-class electrolyzer for decentralized green hydrogen. Five 25 kW AEM Stacks work on one shared balance of plant, so a single stack can be serviced while the other four keep producing.

It delivers up to 24.1 Nm³/h (2.16 kg/h) of hydrogen at 51.3 kWh/kgH₂ system efficiency, and its 12 to 100% operating range is built to follow variable solar and wind rather than a fixed load.

AEM Flex 120
Production rate
24.1 Nm³/h (2.16 kg/h)
System efficiency

Datasheet
Get a quote
_The AEM Flex 120 at a glance
Modular stack architecture

The system is built from five identical 25 kW AEM Stacks. Each stack is monitored independently and can be isolated for maintenance while the remaining stacks continue producing hydrogen.

Follows variable renewable power

Operating from 12 to 100% of nominal flow and reaching full production in just 225 seconds from hot standby, the system adapts to changing solar and wind generation instead of curtailing renewable energy.

Purity matched to your offtake

Choose the hydrogen purity your application requires: 99.5% in the base configuration, 99.95% with the optional chiller, or up to 99.999% with the optional dryer, at outlet pressures of up to 31 barg.

_Your benefits

Efficient hydrogen production that keeps running despite stack maintenance and variable renewable power.

51.3 kWh/kgH₂ system efficiency: including all utilities inside the battery limits, at full load in the base configuration.
12 to 100% operating range: the system follows renewable power instead of requiring a steady input.
Five independently monitored stacks: isolate one for maintenance without stopping the other four.
Fully automatic operation: managed by the onboard PLC and Enapter control algorithm.
Compact 6 × 2.5 m footprint: including the dryer and water treatment, for indoor installation.
AEM Flex 120 green hydrogen applications
Process heat

Companies using natural gas for process heat are swapping to green hydrogen to fire up their furnaces. The AEM Flex 120 lets brick, ceramics and plastics makers reduce operational costs over time via gas blending, work towards eliminating fossil fuels dependency and establish their sustainability leadership.

Pilot refueling stations

Designed for efficiency and scalability, our flexible electrolyzer enables on-site hydrogen production from fluctuating renewable energy, meeting the demands of pilot projects and the next stages of growth. Reduce reliance on external suppliers, and pave the way for a sustainable hydrogen-driven future.

Energy storage

From peak shaving to long-term storage strategies, this electrolyzer offers a versatile solution harnessing excess energy to produce hydrogen. Companies are empowered to put their decarbonization and self-sufficiency plans into action; energy developers get the most value for grids and communities.

Industrial use

Green hydrogen is replacing grey hydrogen as an industrial feedstock to make foodstuffs, chemicals like ammonia and methane, and more. Our AEM Flex 120 helps industrial firms to rapidly pilot their green hydrogen production and use, opening the door to rapid scaling and full replacement of grey H2.

Make up to 491.6 Nm³/h of green hydrogen an hour (44.2 kg/h) with our 2.5 MW AEM Electrolyzer – or start with our 500 kW version. Both with 99.999% hydrogen purity.

_Scale up green H2 production from intermittent renewable energy  
Maximum uptime

Resilience you can rely on: The modular design removes bottlenecks and single points of failure, all the way from AEM stacks to balance of plant. Enjoy maximum uptime, even when servicing: Work on affected AEM Stacks while others still produce green hydrogen.

Top operational flexibility

AEM Stack electrolyzer cores are the heart of our green hydrogen generators. Our AEM Nexus has hundreds, mounted in stacks of 10. Each stack ramps up or down separately to get the most out of your renewable energy at any load, delivering exceptional operational flexibility of 1-100%.

Straightforward operation

This containerized electrolyzer offers you quick and straightforward setup so you can focus on making and using your green gas. Software control as well as simplified servicing with easily swappable electrolyzer stacks streamline your operations.

_Your benefits
Unlock the future of clean energy with the AEM Nexus by Enapter. 

Designed for efficiency and scalability, it provides a reliable solution to meet the growing demand for sustainable hydrogen production:

World’s first megawatt-class AEM Electrolyzer
Operational flexibility
High degree of redundancy
Rapid reaction times to variable renewables
AEM Nexus green hydrogen applications
Renewable energy storage

Excellent solution for developers, utilities & communities: Get the most from fluctuating renewables with green H2 storage for grid balancing, microgrids, curtailed power and supply of green gas. Unlock power-to-X, power-to-gas, commercial supply, heating & cooling use cases.

Industrial applications

Your key product to replace grey H2 and natural gas: Use it for green ammonia production, process heat for bricks and tiles, as a carrier gas for semiconductors, in blast furnace injection for green steel, renewable methanol, biofuel/biogas production, as well as in glass annealing or as a chemical feedstock.

Hydrogen refueling stations

For those with private FCEV fleets or commercial users: Our containerized systems for on-site green hydrogen production enable you to replace grey hydrogen supply, make the switch from conventional combustion engine vehicles or make your own synthetic fuels and e-fuels.

Energy self-sufficiency

Use green hydrogen to unlock back-up energy, replace polluting diesel generators, research H2 solutions and energy independence, become completely energy self-sufficient, as well as unlock both on-grid and decentralized micro-grids.

AEM Rheos 20
_AEM Rheos 20

Our AEM Rheos 20 is a full-scope, skid-mounted 20 MW hydrogen plant designed for industrial-scale green hydrogen production. Six production trains share the transformers, rectifiers, water treatment, electrolyte loop, hydrogen purification and plant control needed to run and condition the plant, so a single train can be serviced while the other five keep producing.

The reference configuration produces 4,000 Nm³/h (approximately 362 kg/h) of hydrogen at 51.4 kWh/kgH₂ system efficiency, across a 1 to 100% operating range, on a 1,250 m² footprint.

AEM Rheos 20
Production rate
4,000 Nm³/h
System efficiency
51.4 kWh/kgH₂
Operational flexibility
1% to 100%
Hydrogen purity
up to 99.999%
Outlet pressure
up to 31 barg
Datasheet
Discuss your project
_The AEM Rheos 20 at a glance
Maintenance without a plant shutdown

Six production trains run in three rows. Each train can be isolated for service while the other five keep producing, so maintenance never takes the whole plant offline.

One control system for the whole plant

The CoreKraft™ EMS coordinates all six trains as a single asset across a 1 to 100% operating range, so plant output follows available renewable power instead of running at fixed load.

Delivered as one integrated plant

Transformers, rectifiers, water treatment, electrolyte loop, hydrogen purification and plant control ship as one coordinated 20 MW concept, not six separate packages to integrate on site.

AEM Rheos 20

Key specifications, system architecture and equipment in one concise PDF.

Get the full picture
_Your benefits

The AEM RHEOS 20 is designed to make a 20 MW hydrogen project easier to engineer, install and operate, beyond the headline production figures.

Defined 25 × 50 m reference layout: the 1,250 m² plant arrangement gives an early basis for plot planning, access routes and utility routing.
Ground-level, three-row configuration: the production field is laid out for direct access to the individual equipment trains during inspection and maintenance.
Dedicated rectifier-stack architecture: each rectifier supplies a defined AEM Stack cluster, supporting train-level control and reducing dependencies on a shared DC system.
Centralized plant utilities and electrolyte service: water treatment, cooling, hydrogen purification and the KOH loop are consolidated at defined plant boundaries instead of repeated across every production block.
Unified plant control: equipment control, supervisory operation and site safety signals are coordinated through one plant-level control architecture.
